articles.title: The oxygen cold trap in protoplanetary discs
articles.summary: The diffusive transport of oxygen in protoplanetary discs followed by sequestration into ice in the midplane, a process known as the cold trap, can substantially alter the chemical environment where planets form. This paper presents a new time-dependent modelling framework that allows us to consistently simulate kinetic gas-phase chemistry, ice growth and desorption, turbulent diffusive mixing, and gravitational settling of icy particles with a changing particle size distribution over million-year timescales in one-dimensional vertical columns. Applying our model to a T Tauri disc across radii from 1 to 100 au reveals that vertical cold trapping becomes an effective mechanism once the diffus

articles.title: Screening of New Abelian Long-Range Forces
articles.summary: We study how bounds on new $U(1)$ long-range forces, resulting from gauging the Standard Model symmetries $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$, $a,b=e,μ,τ$, are modified if the mediator mass is generated by the Higgs mechanism. Large baryonic and leptonic charges of astronomical bodies displace the Higgs field from its vacuum value, resulting in charge screening. Depending on the $U(1)$ Higgs mass, the screening relaxes the bounds on the new force strength and mediator mass from equivalence principle violation and neutrino oscillations experiments, and eliminates the bounds on the muonic $L_μ-L_τ$ force from neutron star binaries.

articles.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
articles.summary: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $ν_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.

articles.title: A Bayesian Approach to Prioritizing the Follow-Up of Near-Earth Objects
articles.summary: We present pneo, a Bayesian classifier that computes the probability that a single-night tracklet belongs to a near-Earth object (NEO), using only its sky position, angular motion, and apparent magnitude. A tracklet does not determine the object's distance or radial velocity, so pneo integrates a model of the Solar System's small-body populations over all bound orbits consistent with it. The result is the exact posterior probability under that model, with no tuned scores or separately chosen priors: its classifications are optimal for the adopted model, and its probabilities are calibrated. articles.title: periapsis: A Comprehensive Orbital Fitting Package
articles.summary: We introduce a new Python package \texttt{periapsis}, which computes posterior distributions for a variety of orbital parameters given astrometric and/or radial velocity data. \texttt{periapsis} not only returns posterior distributions, but also a variety of statistics assessing convergence and fit metrics as well as plotting capabilities for visualizing the orbital systems. In this paper, we describe our various methods for fitting Keplerian orbits to both astrometric and radial velocity data. We then show the breadth of binary systems that \texttt{periapsis} can characterize by comparing our computed parameters with known orbital systems. articles.title: Is Gravitational-Wave Waveform Systematics a Bottleneck for Formation Channel Inferences using Effective-Spin and Mass-Ratio?
articles.summary: Gravitational-wave measurements of the effective spin $χ_\text{eff}$ and mass ratio $q$ help distinguish binary black hole formation channels, motivating a search for structure in the $χ_\text{eff} - q$ plane. However, both these quantities are known to be strongly correlated in GW parameter estimation since both enter the leading-order spin-orbit term together, and thus, the detectors cannot easily tell them apart. In this work, we harness the susceptibility of such measurements to waveform systematics by using injection-recovery studies with NRSur7dq4 as the true signal and SEOBNRv5PHM and IMRPhenomTPHM for parameter inferences. articles.title: NASA's Pandora SmallSat Mission: Gaussian Processes for Simulated Stellar Heterogeneity Corrections under Imperfect Stellar Models
articles.summary: Stellar contamination is the primary bottleneck limiting robust atmospheric characterization of exoplanets orbiting active K- and M-dwarfs with James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) transmission spectroscopy. Launched in January 2026, NASA's Pandora SmallSat mission addresses this challenge through long-term, simultaneous visible photometry and near-infrared spectroscopy of planet-hosting stars, providing the data to disentangle planetary and stellar signals. However, conventional stellar-contamination corrections rely on stellar atmosphere models, making them vulnerable to model inaccuracies that can impede accurate inferences. articles.title: A Large Envelope Can Explain Super-Puffs
articles.summary: Super-puffs are a class of exoplanets with extremely low bulk densities, having masses of a few to tens of Earth masses but radii comparable to that of Jupiter. Observations suggest that these inflated radii can persist for Gyr timescales, even for planets receiving relatively low stellar irradiation. The physical mechanisms responsible for maintaining such large radii, however, remain poorly understood. Here, we model the thermal evolution of super-puffs with substantial H/He envelopes using a one-dimensional planetary structure and cooling model. articles.title: Determining the Spin-down of the White Dwarf in J191213.72-441045.1 using Optical Time-Series Photometry
articles.summary: J191213.72-441045.1 (J1912-4410) is the second white dwarf pulsar to be discovered. These binary systems consist of a white dwarf primary with a cool companion and undergo pulsed emission from radio to X-ray wavelengths. The prototype of the class, AR Scorpii (AR Sco), exhibits a lack of accretion, which led to suggestions that the spin-down of the white dwarf is powering the system's non-thermal emission. However, J1912-4410 displays possible signatures of accretion, which allows for the possibility that its emission may operate via a different mechanism to AR Sco. articles.title: Discovery of Trailing Spiral Dust Alignment in the Dust Polarization of HL Tau at $λ= 2.1$ mm
articles.summary: Polarimetric observations of protoplanetary disks at (sub)millimeter wavelengths constrain dust grain properties, dynamics, and alignment mechanisms. We present new high-resolution ALMA Band 4 (2.1 mm) polarization observations of HL Tau with spatial resolutions of $\sim$0.08$''$ (11.78 au) and $\sim$0.19$''$ (27.99 au). Linearly decomposing the polarization into contributions from dust scattering and thermal emission by aligned grains, we analyze the new Band 4 data and published high-resolution Band 7 (870 $μ$m) observations. articles.title: X-ray Polarization of the Western Lobe of SS 433
articles.summary: SS 433 is a microquasar producing bipolar jets and a Pevatron candidate, known to accelerate particles to very high energies in two extended lobes. The leading or `head' regions of the lobes exhibit hard X-ray emission due to synchrotron radiation and are identified as the acceleration sites. Previous measurements of the eastern head region revealed a high X-ray polarization degree (PD) indicating that the magnetic field has a well ordered component. Here, we present observations of the western head region with the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) analyzed using a technique employing spatial and particle/photon weights. articles.title: An X-ray binary origin for the LHAASO peanut
articles.summary: The LHAASO "peanut" source is a remarkably extended ($\gtrsim$4$^\circ$) ultra-high-energy gamma-ray emitter detected by the LHAASO observatory. While its angular extent and high-energy spectrum require a Galactic origin, its location at a Galactic latitude of $\approx$-17$^\circ$ limits the possible known counterparts to a nearby millisecond pulsar. However, models accounting for the emission solely with this pulsar require the transport properties to operate near extreme parameter limits. We propose an alternative explanation where the peanut source is produced through the past activity of a now quiescent X-ray binary located at a distance of 1-2 kpc. articles.title: A search and multi-frequency study of curved parsec-scale jets in active galaxies
articles.summary: Very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations show that a fraction of active galactic nucleus (AGN) jets exhibit pronounced apparent bending on parsec scales, potentially strongly enhanced by projection effects. While individual sources have been studied in detail, the statistical properties of curved jets and the physical mechanisms responsible for their morphology remain poorly constrained. We aim to select a statistically robust sample of AGNs with significantly curved parsec-scale jets and to constrain the physical mechanisms responsible for jet bending. We analyse 123 456 VLBI images of 17 478 AGNs collected by the public Astrogeo database. After filtering for extended structure

articles.title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
articles.summary: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. articles.title: Investigating the Neupert Effect with HEL1OS/Aditya-L1
articles.summary: We investigate the Neupert effect in solar flares using broadband hard X-ray observations from the HEL1OS instrument onboard Aditya-L1. By separating thermal and non-thermal components from HEL1OS spectrograms, we analyse a sample of 312 flares observed between November 2023 and May 2026. We find that the soft X-ray flux is strongly correlated with the time-integrated hard X-ray emission, with a median correlation coefficient of 0.984, indicating that Neupert-like behaviour is nearly ubiquitous in flares with detectable non-thermal emission. articles.title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
articles.summary: Superfluids, in a spinning-down container with pinning centres, exhibit sudden collective migration of quantized vortices. The onset, progress, and termination of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we show that: 1) the first exodus of vortices occurs when a sector of the vortex array, having a minimum opening angle, is vacated close to the wall; 2) driven by this exodus, the superfluid flow near the boundary continually decreases in strength and arrests the exit; and 3) the resultant depletion region has well-defined dimensions---governed primarily by the critical unpinning velocity, the container size, and the initial rotation rate---that limit the angular momentum transferred to

articles.title: A comparative analysis of the presence of haze in sub-Neptunes observed with JWST
articles.summary: Photochemical hazes have been proposed to explain the diversity of sub-Neptune transmission spectra, with early HST observations suggesting a temperature-dependent trend in aerosol opacity. However, JWST observations reveal a more heterogeneous picture. Here, we perform a consistent atmospheric retrieval analysis of eight moderately irradiated JWST-observed sub-Neptunes, LP 791-18 c, TOI-1231 b, TOI-732 c, TOI-270 d, GJ 1214 b, GJ 9827 d, GJ 3090 b, and TOI-421 b, using experimentally derived haze optical properties. articles.title: TeV Gamma-Ray Transparency Bounds on Neutrinos and Axions
articles.summary: Multi-TeV gamma rays propagating over cosmological distances measure the extragalactic background light (EBL) through attenuation by electron--positron pair production. This is particularly valuable in the infrared, where the EBL is difficult to measure directly. Since the growing sample of observed multi-TeV photons provides tight constraints on the EBL photon intensity, this, in turn, constrains new particles that radiatively decay into meV--eV photons. We set the first TeV-transparency bounds on active-neutrino electromagnetic transition moments, obtain new constraints on radiatively decaying sterile neutrinos, and derive competitive limits on the axion--photon coupling.

articles.title: On the potential of widening the band of X-ray polarimetry
articles.summary: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has made X-ray polarimetry a routine astrophysical diagnostic, but its sensitivity is confined to the 2-8 keV band, where the photoelectric effect in a gas is most efficiently exploited. Several of the questions raised by its results, as well as some classical goals of high-energy astrophysics, require polarimetry below 2~keV, to reach the thermal emission of neutron stars, black-hole discs and blazars, and above 8~keV, where reflection, cyclotron lines and the non-thermal emission of supernova remnants, pulsar wind nebulae and magnetars can be isolated. articles.title: Super-Eddington Neutron Star Accretion Columns: Comparing GRRMHD Simulations with Spectral Models
articles.summary: The geometry and structure of neutron star accretion columns affect the X-ray emission in super-Eddington accreting systems. We perform four axisymmetric general relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations of super-Eddington accretion onto magnetized neutron stars with the maximum surface magnetic fields ranging from $3\times10^{10}$ to $1\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{G}$. We measure the column width and estimate the characteristic radiation shock heights from the flow velocity and velocity gradient. articles.title: MINDS: The mid-infrared spectrum of the disk, jets, and winds of DG Tau
articles.summary: DG Tau is one of the best-studied young stellar objects in transition from a Class I protostar to a T Tauri star. It is no longer embedded in a dense molecular cloud, but still reveals features that are commonly seen in protostars at earlier evolutionary stages. DG Tau hosts a protoplanetary disk and two energetic jets that can be studied down to the immediate environment of the star and disk at optical, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths. We use the Medium Resolution Spectrometer of MIRI on the James Webb Space Telescope. articles.title: CORALIE Radial Velocity Search for Companions around Evolved Stars (CASCADES) VI. Revised masses and homogeneous estimation of the stellar parameters of 583 red giants
articles.summary: Giant-star radial-velocity surveys allow us to study how the exoplanet population varies with stellar mass and evolution. However, obtaining accurate estimates of stellar masses for such stars is challenging, as methods like isochrone fitting are prone to large errors due to the degeneracy associated with the closeness of isochrones. We provide a homogeneous re-derivation of the stellar parameters of the CASCADES giant-star survey. This includes parameters obtained from spectral energy distribution fitting, as well as an update of the stellar masses using asteroseismology. articles.title: Dynamical conditions for tilting Neptune during planetary migration
articles.summary: Giant planets are expected to form with near-zero obliquities, so that their current tilts must be the result of some post-formation processes. Capture into spin-orbit resonances has been shown to provide a viable mechanism for explaining the current obliquities of Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus. We aim to determine whether specific configurations of a primordial satellite system of Neptune could have enabled the tilting of its spin axis during planetary migration. articles.title: Stellar-evolution systematic biases on $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ constraints from the primordial-black-hole mass gap
articles.summary: The $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ reaction determines helium-burning carbon-oxygen core masses and sets the pair-instability-supernova mass-gap boundary, which limits the maximum mass of stellar-origin primordial black holes. Gravitational-wave population analyses using GWTC-4 report a low-spin-black-hole upper cutoff at $68.5^{+19.8}_{-18.5}\,M_\odot$, implying a low astrophysical S-factor $S_{300}\approx 108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$, in tension with canonical nuclear-astrophysics evaluations. articles.title: Cosmic ray protons from 40 GeV to 10 EeV due to star formation?
articles.summary: The formation of massive stars eventually results in supernovae explosions. Typical supernova remnants (SNRs) accelerate cosmic ray (CR) protons up to $E_{max-p} \sim 10$ TeV; the value of $E_{max-p}$ may reach $\sim 1$ EeV for the case of the hypernovae and/or for a sub-relativistic velocity of the SNR's shock wave. We show that the observable CR proton spectrum in the energy range between 40 GeV and 10 EeV is reasonably well described with a sum of three components that correspond to three distinct SNR populations. articles.title: Critical Eddington luminosity and photon cooling of compact spherical stars
articles.summary: Context. Relativistic corrections to the luminosity have been used for neutron stars of radius greater than $3MG/c^2$ in studies of X-ray bursts. However, there is no fundamental limit that excludes the existence of more compact massive objects with a physical surface, fluid or solid. Aims. We aim to discuss critical "Eddington" luminosity for spherical stars that have a surface within the sphere of unstable circular photon orbits (photon sphere). Methods. articles.title: A homogeneous mass campaign of transiting sub-Neptunes around FGK stars
articles.summary: Sub-Neptunes are among the most common planets in our Galaxy, but are still poorly understood. Addressing their origins and compositions requires precise bulk densities, but literature values come from studies using different radial velocity (RV) extraction methods, stellar activity treatments, and statistical frameworks, which introduces systematic biases that can lead to spurious conclusions in population-level analyses. We conducted a systematic and homogeneous mass-measurement campaign for 12 sub-Neptune systems observed by Kepler and K2, selected for their absent or poorly constrained masses ($σ_{M_p}/M_p > 25\%$). articles.title: Kepler-404: A near-resonant pair of sub-Neptunes. Reinterpreting a false-positive signal with the novel detection method RIVERS.radon
articles.summary: According to the current understanding of planet formation and evolution, (near)-resonant systems should be a common occurrence in nature. However, pairs of planets with period ratios close to commensurability are rarely observed. In this paper, we discuss how observational bias caused by transit timing variations (TTVs) can affect the detection of low signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) planets in transit surveys, playing a role in the lack of representation of these systems. articles.title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
articles.summary: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. articles.title: The 2026 iron meteorite fall near Zadzim (Poland) and atmospheric ablation of iron meteoroids
articles.summary: Understanding the process of penetration of cosmic material through the Earth's atmosphere is important for linking the atmospheric and ground effects with the properties of original bodies. It has been shown previously that the main process affecting the fate of stony impactors is atmospheric fragmentation. Much less is known about iron impactors,mainly because the scarcity of data about actual iron meteorite falls. Here we present the trajectory, dynamics, light curve, spectrum, and orbit of a fireball which occurred on April 17, 2026, over Poland and was observed by the European Fireball Network and the Skytinel Network. articles.summary: Very Large Telescope, Keck I, and Gemini North photometry of 2026 QQ$_8$ on November 7-21 gives Sloan Digital Sky Survey-equivalent colors $g-r=0.594^{+0.056}_{-0.053}$, $g-i=0.840^{+0.066}_{-0.065}$, and $i-z=-0.104^{+0.067}_{-0.057}$ mag. articles.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
articles.summary: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. articles.title: Probabilistic, facility-specific prioritisation of temperate exoplanets for atmospheric characterisation with JWST and the ELT
articles.summary: Deciding which temperate exoplanets to observe first matters for JWST transit spectroscopy and for planned ELT reflected-light instruments, yet signal-to-noise metrics ignore habitability and similarity indices ignore observability. articles.title: The Gamma-ray Luminosity Function of Fermi BL Lacertae Objects
articles.summary: We have used the largest sample of gamma-ray-selected Fermi BL Lacertae objects (1035 BL Lacs) ever used to determine the luminosity function and its evolution through cosmic time. This sample has its survey biases and selection effects well studied and a robust calculation of its detection efficiency. It spans a large range in luminosity ($L_{γ,min}$ = $5.71\times10^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and $L_{γ,max}$ = $1.76\times10^{48}$ erg s$^{-1}$) and redshift ($ 0 < z \lesssim 4 $). articles.title: Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems
articles.summary: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the $f$-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. articles.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
articles.summary: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. articles.title: Selection-aware inference of supernova kicks
articles.summary: Observed compact objects (isolated or in binaries) used to infer natal kicks are selected by class membership, which depends on disruption, subsequent evolution, and discovery. Ignoring this selection can bias the inferred kicks. To demonstrate this bias in a comprehensive inference framework, we construct a differentiable model for key components of binary evolution, including correlated remnant-mass and kick prescriptions as well as survival probabilities. articles.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
articles.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. articles.title: Dawn of the Gaia Era: Revisiting Cold Jupiters Orbiting M Dwarfs with Astrometry+Doppler Data Joint Analysis
articles.summary: We perform a joint analysis of ground-based radial velocities (RVs), Hipparcos Intermediate Astrometric Data, and two-epoch Gaia astrometry for known M dwarfs hosting cold Jupiters discovered through long-term spectroscopic monitoring. Among a sample of 25 planets in 19 systems, we derive robust absolute masses and orbital solutions for 13 planets in 11 systems with companion inclination uncertainties lower than 30 degrees. These include first mass measurements for five planets: GJ 328b, GJ 649b, GJ 849b and c, and GJ 9066c. We also reclassify one object, HIP 79431B, as a brown dwarf. articles.title: Radial and vertical structure of accretion discs around magnetized stars
articles.summary: The ubiquity of accretion discs around magnetized stars motivates studies of the structure of these discs, in particular in whether the external magnetic field changes the radial and vertical profiles of pressure, temperature, and other quantities. We study the effects of the magnetic field of a central star on a steady accretion disc under the assumption that the magnetic field of the central star is able to partially penetrate the disc, with a degree of penetration quantified by a single parameter. articles.title: Early Realignment of Eccentric Planetary Orbits without Orbital Decay
articles.summary: Warm Jupiters are, on average, more closely aligned with their host stars than hot Jupiters, even at high eccentricities. articles.title: Search for Axion-like Particles using Blazar Observations with the HAWC Observatory
articles.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can mix with photons in astrophysical magnetic fields, modifying the propagation of very-high-energy gamma rays from distant blazars and producing an energy-dependent enhancement of the observed flux relative to the standard expectation from absorption on the extragalactic background light (EBL). articles.title: Constraining Gamma-Ray Emission Beyond the TOV Limit: A Targeted Fermi-GBM Search for Counterparts to 39 LVK Gravitational-Wave Candidates in GWTC-5.0
articles.summary: We present a systematic search for sub-threshold gamma-ray counterparts within a one-day time window of 161 gravitational-wave (GW) events from the GWTC-5.0 catalog, whose inferred source masses exceed the adopted Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) limit, using the Gamma-ray Targeted Search (GTS) pipeline. articles.title: Archival X-Ray Observations of the Eclipsing Algol-type Binary TV~Cassiopeiae
articles.summary: TV~Cassiopeiae (TV~Cas) is an eclipsing Algol-type binary with a B9\,V primary and an evolved late-type secondary in a 1.81-day orbit. We examine six serendipitous Chandra and two XMM-Newton observations spanning 2003--2012. The supplied Chandra spectra show thermal plasma near 1~keV and sub-solar fitted abundances, with an additional hotter component in one observation. EPIC-pn fits improve substantially with two temperatures: approximately 0.74/1.39~keV in 2003 and 0.87/2.16~keV in 2012. articles.title: Reconstructing the depth of first interaction in extensive air showers from fluorescence detector profiles with a physics-motivated neural network
articles.summary: We present a physics-motivated neural network that reconstructs, event by event, the depth of the first interaction of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays from longitudinal profiles measured by fluorescence detectors. The network couples a convolutional encoder to a decoder that implements the Gaisser-Hillas function and predicts quantiles of the target, providing a per-event uncertainty estimate. It is trained and evaluated on four million proton- and iron-induced showers between $10^{18}$ and $10^{20}$ eV, simulated with the hadronic interaction models EPOS LHC-R and Sibyll 2.3d and processed by an end-to-end simulation of the fluorescence detector response. articles.title: Carving the Neptunian desert as a function of stellar mass and lifetime XUV irradiation
articles.summary: The Neptunian desert is a prominent feature in the exoplanet population, thought to arise from both XUV-driven photoevaporation and tidal circularisation following high-eccentricity migration. However, the extent to which each mechanism contributes, and where, remains uncertain. We examine the desert as a function of stellar type as a test of these mechanisms. We determine the desert boundaries for subsamples of F, G, K, and M-hosted planets for radius against period, semi-major axis, bolometric instellation, and lifetime XUV irradiation. articles.title: What determines the properties of Population III binaries?
articles.summary: Population~III binaries may provide a gravitational-wave probe of the first stellar populations. Uncertain initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions complicate predictions of their remnant masses, birth orbits and formation spins. Varying these model evolutionary parameters (MEPs) jointly is needed to identify which MEPs shape each property and whether their effects persist among binaries that merge. We use \textsc{StarTrack} to evolve $2\times10^6$ initial binaries per model across 1152 configurations spanning eight MEPs. articles.title: 2026 QQ8: Earth's temporary flyby of maximum lunation
articles.summary: Aims: On a rare occasion, asteroids are temporarily captured by the Earth to become the planet's interim companions. The discovery of asteroid 2026~QQ$_8$ provided an opportunity to study this class of objects, adding to the sparse discovery catalogue of Earth's temporary companions. Methods: We performed astrometric, photometric, and dynamical studies of 2026~QQ$_8$, and measured its solar radiation pressure signal to discern between a natural and an artificial origin. articles.title: Disrupted stars and captured compact objects: Combining observations from multiple messengers to infer the population of massive black holes
articles.summary: Massive black holes (MBHs) are found in galactic centres, but their formation and evolution remain elusive. Tidal disruption events (TDEs) and extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) both arise from stellar dynamics in the nuclear star clusters around MBHs, and are observed with electromagnetic surveys and gravitational waves, respectively. To overcome the scarcity of coincident detections, we formulate how to combine gravitational-wave detections from LISA-EMRIs with observations from ZTF-TDEs to measure properties of the MBH population. articles.title: Probing for relativistic outflows in the Ultraluminous X-ray pulsar RX J0209.6-7427
articles.summary: Context. Relativistic winds have been observed in Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs), but their detection at large distances remains limited. Galactic neutron stars accreting matter from Be-star companions provide a valuable opportunity to improve our understanding of these outflows. Aims. RX J0209.6-7427 is a Be-XRB, powered by a neutron star with a spin period of 9.3 seconds, that underwent an outburst in 2019, exceeding a bolometric luminosity of $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$ at its peak. articles.title: Nuclear Precision and Multimessenger Constraints on Neutron-Star Structure
articles.summary: Neutron-star cores retain structural freedom beyond the constraints supplied by nuclear measurements. We quantify this freedom through an observable-dependent variance ceiling and identify radius--Love compensation as a mechanism suppressing nuclear constraints on tides. Across four data-conditioned equation-of-state families, a pulsar radius measured to 0.3 km paired with a binary tide measured to 10\% removes 44--68\% of the current logarithmic Love-number variance. The framework connects laboratory precision and complementary stellar measurements to core structure.

articles.title: Hints of planet formation in progress around DR Tau from observations with LBT SHARK-NIR and SHARK-VIS
articles.summary: Protoplanetary disks are the primary sites of planet formation. However, the direct imaging of protoplanets still embedded within their parental disks remains a significant challenge, with only a small number of confirmed detections to date and several candidates awaiting verification. We search for embedded planets in the protoplanetary disk of the young star DRTau by targeting accretion signatures from forming sub-stellar objects. Using narrow-band imaging, we observe both visible Halpha and near-infrared Paschen-beta (Pabeta) emission to identify actively accreting companions. articles.title: Nuclear Urca cooling in magnetar crust and anomalous heating
articles.summary: We present a new result that the nuclear Urca process in magnetars, associated with ultrastrong magnetic field, dramatically alters the neutrino cooling efficiency to support higher surface temper ature, which is not common in ordinary neutron stars. A new formalism for neutrino luminosity accommodating finite temperature on top of magnetic field is extended with the use of realistic nuclear structure inputs for the Urca pair 29Na-29Mg. articles.title: The GAPS programme at TNG. LXXXIII. Orbital refinement and atmospheric investigation of TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b)
articles.summary: TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b) is a highly irradiated ultra-hot Jupiter on a strongly misaligned orbit, a benchmark target for atmospheric and dynamical studies. We comprehensively characterise the TOI-1518 system by refining its orbital and physical parameters, and by investigating the chemical composition of the planetary atmosphere through transmission spectroscopy. articles.title: Modelling scintillation in Fast Radio Bursts
articles.summary: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are bright, ms-duration, extragalactic radio transients. Propagation through inhomogeneities in the ionised medium produces scintillation, observed as frequency-dependent intensity variations in their spectra, with bright patches, called scintles. The characteristic scintillation bandwidth probes scattering material along the line of sight. Measuring this scale can be challenging when the observing bandwidth of the burst spectra contains a few scintles.
